account:
So far I have no concrete evidence of anything secret or unusual in town. My morning market conversations yielded no news. The innkeeper reported eight fresh loaves, no lodging requests and no concerns; the innkeeper wants advance notice of visitors or gatherings. Freight says the warehouse was empty this morning, no unusual shipments or quay concerns were observed, and the ferry is available. Freight wants destinations and deadlines for any authorized cargo. These sound like ordinary efforts to find work and coordinate business, not evidence of a hidden undertaking.

The builder reported the bridge, bakery approach, east landing approach and quay road passable, with no verified damage or immediate danger, though this was not structural certification. I have now explicitly approved a two-emerald closer visual bridge inspection, with a written report due tomorrow at noon and payment upon delivery, excluding repairs and purchases. There was some confusion: the builder initially responded as though no further work had been commissioned, so I repeated the approval before leaving. I did not make out the replies during my departure and cannot yet confirm how they recorded it.

The secretary reported no receipts or expenses reported to them. Several of the secretary's earlier remarks were unintelligible to me; that is a gap in my knowledge, not proof of concealment. My appointment book specified tea with the neighbour at an east-bank dockside cottage but no exact address. I have reached the cottage a little late, at 15:24, and can see the neighbour nearby. This is an opportunity to keep my appointment and hear local news. I remain curious about my feeling that something is happening without me, but I have not identified participants, a plan, or a purpose beyond the ordinary town business described above.
